disease_label_per_paper: Type II mixed cryoglobulinaemia vasculitis secondary to marginal zone lymphoma
presentation_summary: 63-year-old man with congenital single kidney and end-stage renal failure on hemodialysis had recurrent vasculitic presentations including leukocytoclastic lower-limb rash, visual symptoms, abdominal pain, fevers, weight loss, digital ischemia, intestinal vasculitis, and pulmonary hemorrhage.
He had long-standing hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, prior stroke, and later diagnosis of indolent marginal zone lymphoma.

During abdominal-pain presentations, labs included hemoglobin 109 g/L, WBC 5.8 x10^9/L, platelets 359 x10^9/L, albumin 27 g/L, creatinine 716 umol/L, CRP 86 with reference <5, C3 1.01 g/L, and C4 0.09 g/L.
Later presentations showed CRP >200 with reference <5 and procalcitonin 2.75 ug/L, hepatosplenomegaly, bowel wall thickening, and marginal-zone lymphoma workup.

At diagnosis of type II cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, serum cryoglobulins were positive with cryocrit 5%, C4 0.03 g/L, RF 499 IU/mL, HBV/HCV antibodies negative, and jejunal and skin biopsies showed vasculitis.

He was treated with IV methylprednisolone, high-dose oral prednisolone, rituximab, IVIG replacement, and later plasma exchange for presumed vasculitis-associated pulmonary hemorrhage; cryocrit fell to <1% and C4 rose to 0.75 g/L after final rituximab.

actual_treatment: IV methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for 3 days
oral prednisolone 75 mg daily on a weaning protocol
intravenous immunoglobulin replacement for severe hypogammaglobulinemia
five sessions of centrifugal plasma exchange separate from hemodialysis with warmed 4% albumin substitution fluid

clinical_course_events.source_text_value: October 2019 leukocytoclastic vasculitis rash on legs treated with corticosteroids
multiple presentations with abdominal pain; jejunal biopsy demonstrated intestinal vasculitis
bilateral non-blanching lower limb rash and cyanotic discoloration of fingertips, especially right second, third, and fourth digits
after three doses of rituximab, he developed hemoptysis; pulmonary hemorrhage was presumed cryoglobulinaemia vasculitis associated and treated with plasma exchange
after final dose of rituximab, cryocrit improved to <1% and C4 increased to 0.75 g/L
he has had no relapses of cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis since treatment and marginal zone lymphoma is monitored as outpatient

quality_warnings: Renal labs are preserved but interpreted in the context of pre-existing end-stage renal failure on hemodialysis.
CRP units in the source text appear as mg/mL, but values are structured as mg/L because the reference range is listed as <5.
No unreported bowel wall thickness, exact fever temperature, or exact post-treatment renal values were invented.
